messages:
Anita R.: Quick follow-up to the RFC — proposing a 'hemisphere split' for the runtime stack (control vs hotpath) to shrink blast radius and make ownership clearer. High level: two coarse domains, each with its own deploy cadence and safety net. Thoughts?
Mike L.: I like the mental model. Can you sketch failure modes? especially cascading KV cache invalidation between hemispheres.
Anita R.: Good call. Failure modes I'm worried about:
- control -> hotpath lag causing stale routing decisions
- duplicate prefix caches if we accidentally double-cache on both sides
- rollout mismatches causing shape drift (schema, header expectations)
Also thinking: a lightweight contract shim in the RPC layer and a canary by-traffic gate.
Jordan: How heavy is that shim? If it's too heavyweight we recreate the facade problem.
Anita R.: Shim intention: tiny, versioned, and just enough to translate route headers + token validation. Equivalent to ~120 LOC in go/ts, not a full adapter. It's only for the cutover window.
Sophia: What about telemetry? We need per-request lineage so we can trace where a token originated and which hemisphere served the cached response. Otherwise debugging will suck.
Anita R.: Agreed — plan is to add `x-hem-orig` header and emit a minimal span tag `hemisphere=control|hot` so trace filters can pivot. Also separate cost/latency dashboards per-hem.
Mike L.: Rollout strategy idea: start with read-only hotpath in the new hemisphere, route 5% of non-critical traffic for 48h, then bump to 20% if no regressions. Canary monitor: P95 latency, 4xx/5xx deltas, and token-unit cost delta.
Jordan: For tech-debt paydown: can we use the split to decommission the old `session-mangler` library? It's the biggest pile of runtime hacks.
Anita R.: Yes — plan is to extract the stable bits into `session-core` and mark the rest as legacy. We'll gate new hemisphere on `session-core` only. That gives us a natural removal path for mangler.
Sophia: Danger: cross-hem db migrations. If both need schema changes, ordering will be a pain. Any ideas to mitigate?
Anita R.: Two mitigations: 1) prefer additive migrations (new columns + backfill) during the split; 2) use a migration feature-flag toggled via the control hemisphere, with automatic fallback to old read path if backfill incomplete.
Mike L.: Also add a migration smoke-run in staging that exercises both hemispheres simultaneously. If we can't replicate cross-hem timing, we won't rollout.
Jordan: Security question: KMS/HSM access — will the hotpath have the same key scopes? We should minimize cross-hem secrets to reduce blast radius.
Anita R.: Hotpath will have narrow decrypt-only keys; control hemisphere keeps signing keys. We update IAM + KMS policies as part of the cutover playbook.
eng-oncall-bot: Deploy queued: hemisphere-shim-v1 -> staging at 2026-04-02T14:18:00Z
Sophia: Nice. Can we add an observability checklist to the playbook? e.g., trace header present, fallback rate under 0.5%, cache duplication < 2x, request tail p99 under SLO+30ms.
Anita R.: Adding checklist now. Also adding a rollback hypothesis section: if fallback > 1% for 30min then revert traffic to legacy hemisphere.
Mike L.: One more ops note — prepare a lightweight 'stitchback' endpoint that can replay a sample of requests across hemispheres for offline diffs. Will help with subtle behavior drift.
Anita R.: Good idea. I'll add a `stitchback/replay` job to the runbook that pulls random 1k requests/day (sanitized) and runs diff checks.
Jordan: TL;DR: +1 for hemisphere split if shims are tiny, telemetry lineage is solid, and migration/backout gates are explicit.
Sophia: +1, adding the observability tasks to my sprint.
Anita R.: Thanks all — I'll post the updated playbook and a minimal cutover checklist by EOD. :thumbsup:
Mike L.: Thanks — will review the playbook and drop comments inline. :eyes:
